subject.title: Feature Request: Masked Secrets - Prevent Agent from Accessing Raw API Keys

question: Should OpenClaw guarantee that agent-controlled tools and subprocesses cannot access raw credentials, and which enforceable boundary should provide that guarantee?
rationale: The existing runtime intentionally trusts same-user processes, while arbitrary commands can exfiltrate any injected value; choosing process isolation, capability mediation, or an external-only boundary changes the core security and plugin contract.

options.title: Adopt a capability boundary
options.body: Design a core-owned broker or isolated executor where agents request allowlisted capabilities and raw credentials are injected only after authorization outside the agent-readable process.

options.title: Support external isolation only
options.body: Keep SecretRefs scoped to configuration-at-rest protection and document plugins, OS user isolation, and external gateways as the supported agent credential boundary.

options.title: Narrow to constrained tools
options.body: Add credential injection only for explicitly declared tools and destinations, leaving arbitrary shell commands outside the guarantee.

recommendation.title: Adopt a capability boundary
recommendation.body: Design a core-owned broker or isolated executor where agents request allowlisted capabilities and raw credentials are injected only after authorization outside the agent-readable process.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice defines the repository's credential isolation and threat-model boundary across secrets, execution, plugins, and gateway behavior.
